chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Imran al-Sabi'i, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Every person who does not love for the sake of the Religion and does not hate for the sake of the Religion, has no Religion.

key_terms.فَلَا دِينَ لَهُ: so there is no Religion for him
key_terms.يُبْغِضْ: to hate (for the sake of God/Religion)
key_terms.يُحِبَّ: to love (for the sake of God/Religion)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for having true religion according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the Shia doctrine of al-Muwaddah wa al-Mubahadah bi-l-Din, emphasizing that religious identity is defined by objective criteria rather than subjective preference. It establishes that true faith necessitates aligning one's affection and animosity with divine will, a concept central to distinguishing the faithful from the hypocrites in Shia theological discourse.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Imran Al Sabi’e, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Everyone who does not love upon the Religion and does not hate upon the Religion, so there is no Religion for him’.
en.sarwar: 16. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Imran al-Subay’i from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever does not love because of religion and does not hate because of religion has no religion.”
